title: Method Selection Guidelines
body:
Method Selection Guidelines. Method Selection Guidelines is a record in the Research Methodology and Experiment Design Database. Documents research methods and experiment designs, with controls, variables, and analysis plans per design. It belongs to the shared capability infrastructure: it is not a disconnected list, but one catalog entry in a system where databases link to each other, share search and validation rules, and can be checked against related databases. Its teaching ladder rank is simple, so it is placed where a reader working from simple records toward compounded and most complex records will meet it at the right point in the sequence.

Scope and schema. The scope of this record is exactly one well defined piece of knowledge acquisition: method selection guidelines. Every record in this database carries the same schema fields: id, title, scope, schema, method, checks, demo, evidence, version, and provenance. The scope field states what the record covers and what it deliberately does not cover; the schema field lists the data the record must contain before it is accepted; the method field names the procedure applied; the checks field lists the acceptance tests the result must pass. A record missing any required field is rejected at build time, not published with a gap.

Method. The working method for this record is Method selection and experiment design. First, the question is written down in one sentence so its scope is clear. Second, the relevant inputs and assumptions are listed, including anything that is not yet known. Third, the method is applied in order, with each intermediate result kept visible rather than hidden inside a single final number. Fourth, the result is compared against an independent check, such as a second calculation, a boundary case, or a review of the assumptions. Retrieval was measured at build time on this database's own records: every record title query returns its record, and every record loads and parses.
